title: Sultanate of Sambaliung
capsule: The Sultanate of Sambaliung was a successor Malay polity on the Berau River in northeastern Borneo (modern East Kalimantan), founded around 1810–1830 when the Berau region was reorganized following the decline of the older Berau sultanate. Its capital was at Tanjung Batu. Dutch colonial authorities recognised it as a distinct entity and concluded a contract with Sambaliung around 1850, subordinating it to Netherlands Indies suzerainty. The sultanate persisted in tributary form until Indonesian independence, after which it was dissolved into the administrative framework of East Kalimantan province.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Documentation is thin and largely confined to Dutch colonial administrative records and Indonesian-language secondary sources; territorial boundaries are poorly defined for the early period.
